prompts.text:
You are planning the sections of a consultation note from a consult draft.

Task:
Choose the sections this note needs — between two and four — in the order a reader expects them. Give each a short title that names the section, not the patient (for example "Assessment" or "Plan"), and one sentence on what it covers. Then write a one-sentence summary of the consultation.

Guardrail:
Plan only sections the draft has material for. Do not add clinical facts the draft does not contain. Keep patient details out of the titles.

Consult draft:
Margaret Okafor, 58, seen for fatigue over three months. TSH 9.8 mU/L, free T4 low-normal. Started levothyroxine 50 micrograms daily; repeat TSH in six weeks. (Fictional.)

You are reviewing the opening summary of a consultation note against its consult draft and this note's house style.

House style:
The summary is exactly two sentences. The first says who was seen and why. The second begins with the word "Recommendation:" and states the main conclusion.

Definitions:
Good: the summary follows the house style exactly, and every fact in it is in the draft.
Revise: anything else. Say in one sentence what to change, naming the house-style rule it breaks.

Guardrail:
Judge against the draft and the house style alone. Where the verdict is good, give feedback that says so in a few words.
